see.b: Commonly known as Palace of Fine Arts or Cathedral of Arts in Mexico, host of art events and art exhibitions, along with a number of enormous murals including Diego Rivera's El hombre controlador del universo and Jorge González…
Commonly known as Zócalo, it is one of the largest squares in the world, surrounded by historic buildings, including the City Hall and the Cathedral.

see.n: Catedral Metropolitana de la Ciudad de México
see.b: Next to El Zocalo in the city center. The biggest cathedral in the Americas. Containing many altars, its principal altar is made from solid gold.
A monument in Reforma Avenue that celebrates Mexico's independence in 1810.

Catholicism's holiest place in the Americas, and the destination of pilgrims from all over the world, especially during the yearly celebration on the 12th of December. It is the shrine that guards the poncho of Juan Diego that contains…

The main campus of the Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México, the National Autonomous University of Mexico. Located on Insurgentes Sur Avenue, it is one of the world's largest universities, with more than 270,000 students every…
Historic Colonial Arts district which was home to Frida Kahlo, Leon Trotsky, and Diego Rivera, among others.

The square is surrounded by cafés and restaurants much favored by tourists, and in these and in the square itself groups of musicians play folk music. Most of these groups are "mariachis" from Jalisco, dressed in Charro costume and…
A 12 km long grand avenue built for the Emperor Maximilian's wife in the 19th century. Its name commemorates the liberal reforms of Mexican President Benito Juarez.
It was the first to screen art films, and is known for its forums, retrospectives and homages. It has four screening rooms, a video and a film library, as well as a cafeteria.
For stunning views of the city. Its central location, height (183 m or 597 ft; 45 stories), and history make it one of Mexico City's most important landmarks.

One of the best museums worldwide over, it was built in late 1960s and designed by Pedro Ramírez Vázquez. Notice the huge, impressive fountain in the courtyard. It gathers the best collection of sculptures, jewels and handcrafts from…
Examples of modern, colonial, and pre-Columbian architecture, all around one square.
Here you will find paintings from Frida Kahlo, Leonora Carrington and Remedios Varo, as well as a sculpture garden.

An art philanthropist left her former home, the grand Hacienda La Noria, as a museum featuring the works of her friend Diego Rivera. At least 137 of his works are displayed here, as are 25 paintings of Frida Kahlo. The premises also…
A concert hall and an arts center, it houses some of Mexico's finest murals and the Art Deco interior is worth seeing alone.
A private museum and collection of many well-known European artists, including an extensive selection of works by Auguste Rodin.
Contains the works of Mexican painter, Rufino Tamayo.
Opened in 1992 and is filled with about 1,000 paintings, drawings, and sculptures from notorious artist, Jose Cuevas.

see.n: National History Museum in Chapultepec's Castle
see.b: The Museum's nineteen rooms contain, in addition to a collection of pre-Columbian material and reproductions of old manuscripts, a vast range of exhibits illustrating the history of Mexico since the Spanish conquest.
If you've got kids, they'll love it! Bright, colorful, and filled with educational experiences for children of all ages.
A science museum maintained by UNAM, the largest university in Latin America. Take some time to wander around the Campus.
Contains murals of acclaimed artist, Diego Rivera.
You can see some impressive Diego Rivera frescoes.
There are some of Orozco's best frescoes. The temporary exhibitions are usually very good.
Display the collections of Franz Mayer, it holds Mexico's largest decorative art collection and also hosts temporary exhibits in the fields of design and photography.
Great place to learn about Mexico City's eclectic history.
Contains the ruins and last remnants of the Aztec empire. attached to the huge archeological site where the foundations of the temple were accidentally found in the 1970s.
The San Carlos Museum holds some of Mexico's best paintings and exhibit 15th and 16th century paintings.
The National Art Museum, houses a rich collection of Mexican art ranging from the 16th to the first half of the 20th centuries.
The former house of the painter since she was born to her death, and full of some of her works, and many of her personal artifacts.
An impressive modern representation of Mayan architecture, it houses Diego Rivera’s collection of Aztec and other precolumbian cultures' sculptures.

This was the house where Trotsky lived in exile during the last 1.5 years of his life, and was murdered by one of Stalin's agents. Guided tours are provided by members of the Workers/ Revolutionary Party.

Most Mexican kids receive toys from the Three Wise Men (Reyes Magos). This is a celebration that pays homage to the aforementioned Bible story. To celebrate it the family gather to eat the "Rosca de Reyes", a sort of bundt cake filled…

Each year in February, the world of contemporary art focuses on Mexico City's Art Week when parties, celebrations, special gallery exhibitions and myriad galas take place throughout the city. The event takes place at the same time as…

In the evening, the President of the country (or the city mayor) salutes the crowds from the presidential balcony in the National Palace in the Constitution Square (Zocalo) and shouts the famous "Viva Mexico". The Zocalo (and the rest…

In the morning, there is a military parade that runs across Paseo de la Reforma, turns right at Juarez Avenue which later becomes Madero Street and ends at the Zocalo. 15,000 to 30,000 soldiers of the Mexican Army, Navy and Air Force…

Alebrijes are brightly colored fanciful animal figures that are one of Mexico's most iconic pop art genres. Each year, enormous Alebrijes floats are created and a parade is held along Paseo de la Reforma and then on to the Zocalo. Pink…

Mexico is one of the few countries in the world that celebrates this day (Dia de los Muertos), in which people go to the cemeteries to offer tribute to their departed ones, and decorate their graves with marigolds and bright colors. But…
Largest amusement park in Latin America. The park is fitted with several million-dollar attractions, including Batman the Ride and not for the faint-hearted Medusa Roller Coaster.

Small urban amusement park in the heart of Chapultepec Park. Park entry is free but rides are paid for individually. Includes a giant Ferris wheel with 40 cabins, a large steel roller coaster, a carousel, and swings.

The largest stadium in Latin America is also the eighth biggest soccer stadium in the world. It's the home of El Tri, the Mexico men's national team, and also home to two of the country's most famous soccer top-tier professional clubs:…

Simply known as "Estadio de C.U." Located south of the city, this was the site of the 1968 Olympic opening ceremony. It is home to Club Universidad Nacional, more often known as Pumas, a soccer team operated by the National University…
Modernistic baseball stadium built in 2019 for 20,000 cheering fans. It is home field for the Diablos de Mexico, a Mexican League professional team.
Built in 1962, this 4.4 km track hosts Grand Prix Formula One and other motor racing such as NASCAR and A1-Grand Prix. The next Formula 1 races are 29 October to 1 November 2026.

With a full capacity of 22,300, Arena CDMX hosts indoor sporting events and a wide range of popular music events. It is the home for annual NBA basketball games played in Mexico, and also hosts home games of Capitanes de la Ciudad de…
Mexico City's home for horse racing, both thoroughbreds and quarter-horses. There are races nearly every day, with different zones for different budgets.
The most famous venue for lucha libre.
Another famous venue for lucha libre and boxing.
Opera, traditional Mexican and classical music.
Alternative music and metal.
Home to the Mexico City Symphonic Orchestra.
Home to the UNAM Symphonic Orchestra

see.pr: M$59, free for children under 12 and students with valid ID
see.b: The site of the main Aztec temple of Tenochtitlan, it was destroyed by Spanish conquistadors in 1521, who then promptly erected the Cathedral roughly over it – but not quite. Centuries later, nearly completely forgotten, its actual…

This excellent four-story museum was designed by Mexican architect Pedro Ramírez Vázquez, and built in 1987 to showcase the many artifacts found on the site. Highlights include the Coyolxauhqui disc as well as the many thousands of…

see.pr: Free admission with photo ID (national driver's license is acceptable)
see.b: The palace in its current form began construction in 1693 and served as the Palace of the Viceroy of New Spain until the Mexican War of Independence, when it became the executive seat of the President (though today it is no longer his…

This place is allegedly where the Aztecs found the eagle eating a snake on top of a cactus (nopal), the divine sign of the gods to settle down and establish the city of Tenochtitlán. It features a sculpture by Juan Olaguibel made in 1970.

see.a: Monte de Piedad and Cinco de Mayo
see.b: This building, which was completed in 1758, was built on the grounds of the house of Aztec emperor Moctezuma and later the residence of the Spanish conqueror Hernán Cortés. The building was acquired in 1838 by the Nacional Monte de…

see.n: Casa de la Primera Imprenta de América
see.b: This building, which dates from 1524, housed the first printing press in the New World, which operated from 1539 until 1560. After this time the building was used for a number of purposes until it was restored by the Universidad…
Features an open-air diorama of the old Tenochtitlán.

see.n: Suprema Corte de Justicia de la Nación
see.b: This building was completed in 1945 and was designed by architect Antonio Muñoz Garcia.

The largest cathedral in the American continent. Designed by Claudio de Arcinieaga, construction started in 1537 and lasted for 250 years. Be sure to check out the side chapels where parishioners leave offerings for the various saints.…
A side chapel next to the Cathedral completed in 1769. The façade is an excellent example of Mexican Churrigueresque architecture.
This church was started in the 16th century and completed in the 19th century; it was built in the grounds of the zoo of Aztec Emperor Moctezuma.

see.n: Templo Expiatorio Nacional de San Felipe de Jesús
see.b: Built in 1897 on the site of the former Vasque Church of Aranzazu.
Built in 1678 and refurbished in 1845.

Tucked away on a side street, this very narrow gem of a church was built in the 1770s and is notable for being an outstanding example of Mexican Churrigueresque architecture. Even more remarkable than the façade, however, are the nine…

see.n: Templo y Convento de Regina Coeli
see.b: Huge historic church known for its opulent baroque interior. Part of a large Conceptionist convent founded in 1573. The statues and artwork is spectacular as is the gilded altar.

see.h: public access Mon-Fri 10:30 - 14:00, Sat-Sun mass only, no public tours
see.b: Baroque-style church established by the Jesuit order in the late 16th century and completed in 1610. The church is famous for its extensive art collection, some of which is on display for public viewing in an attached art gallery. The…

Established in 1592, this green garden with fountains and statues is the oldest public park in the Americas. The name comes from álamo, the Spanish word for poplar tree, that were planted here. Much of the current layout of the park,…
The second largest square in Centro Histórico after the Zócalo. It is surrounded by various important buildings such as the Palacio de la Inquisición, Santo Domingo convent and the old Customs House.

This museum managed by the Medicine Faculty of the National University shows the history of health care in Mexico. Features a great replica of an old pharmacy and reconstructed labs of influential medical researchers. Signage is in…
In this beautiful square you can find the statue of Spanish king Charles IV also known as El Caballito (the little horse).

see.pr: Adult M$95; children under 13, people with disabilities, students with a valid I
see.b: Housed in the former Palace of Telecommunications, this beautiful Porfirian-style building was built in 1904 by architect Silvio Contri. The museum presents a permanent collection of paintings and sculptures from the 16th century…

see.h: Guided tours on Sat Sun 11:00 and13:00
see.b: Formerly the Mining College, this building dated from 1792 features an old library and a chapel. It serves as venue for the yearly Mexico City Book Fair.

The temple, like Tenochtitlan's Templo Mayor, was built in several layers and is now the site of continuing archaeological exploration; it occupies the largest amount of area, on the north and west side of the plaza. If you're not…

The colonial church, built by Spaniards immediately after destroying the temple in their conquest of Aztec lands, was constructed using stones "borrowed" from the temple itself. Despite its weathered appearance, the interior is…

eat.b: There is a big variety of street food.
At different times there are other food stalls open.

eat.h: Daily 08:00 - 05:00 (yes, they only close for 3 hours)
eat.b: One of Mexico City's many famous taco stands, Cocuyo's has been featured on international food shows including Anthony Bourdain's No Reservations and the Netflix series, Taco Chronicles. The place has changed since Bourdain visited.…

eat.n: Mercado San Juan Arcos de Belen
eat.b: It is full of food stalls offering all the Mexican favorites. Find the one opposite the small bakers by one of the rear entrances on Calle Delicias, which serves the Torta Cubana. The people running it are amazingly welcoming and the…
Delicious traditional Mexican cuisine at some of the best prices in Centro.

Cozy upstairs restaurant specializing in chiles rellenos, including the national dish of chile en nogada. Very authentic cooking with several regional dishes based on indigenous traditions, and sometimes unusual ingredients that will…

Long-time fixture in the heart of downtown. Traditional homemade Mexican food including fresh baked breads, though the restaurant is historically Chinese and once served hybrid Mexicanized Chinese dishes. The place is known for its…
Generous plates, many of which are ramen. Spicy red chili sauce is provided for people who want to take the flavor up a notch.
Buffet style restaurant with to-go service at 65 pesos, making it very cheap for a lot of food.
Chinese buffet serving lots of food at low prices.
This taco joint is good if you want to try tacos al pastor, as featured in Anthony Bourdain's Mexico show.

This torteria is owned by former luchador Super Astro, and serves not only tortas but also standard Mexican fare. Their enormous torta Super Gladiator is free if you can eat the whole thing in 15 minutes.

This restaurant has been serving Mexican food since the early 1900s and retains the same furniture since then. When you get there, look up to the ceiling, as you will see the famous gun shot accidentally fired by Pancho Villa.

This restaurant is favored by the local Mexican-Lebanese community, many of whom still own the small businesses and textile shops in the immediate area. It serves a range of standard Lebanese dishes, including an excellent mezze.

A newer rooftop establishment with great seating overlooking the Templo Mayor, this restaurant specializes in creative twists to traditional Mexican dishes. It's very popular for lunch, so it's best to arrive early.

Housed in a former inn, this restaurant opened in 1860 and is the oldest restaurant in Mexico City. It serves classic traditional Mexican dishes in a lively atmosphere, and is very popular with residents.

Upscale dining room serving outstanding regional and traditional Mexican cuisine. The restaurant has been a favorite of businessmen and politicos for generations. The food is always excellent, as is the service. They bake their own…
This confectionery shop sells old fashioned sweets. It was established in 1874 and still has its original cabinets from that age.

Elegantly rustic dining room with innovative regional cuisine and a full bar with a variety of mezcals, tequilas, and an excellent wine list featuring many great Baja vintages. Adventurous palates shouild try the carnitas de conejo.
Elegant rooftop restaurant with innovative nuevo Mexican cuisine and spectacular views of the historic downtown area.

Trendy casual restaurant serving traditional Mexican and regional dishes. Great breakfast and interesting dishes at lunch and dinner including nogales en chile, mole and more. Family friendly with affordable prices.
Housed in a former convent, this institution serves up tasty Mexican dishes all day for reasonable prices. It is very popular so arrive early. Menu is in English and Spanish.
Restaurant on the roof of the Hotel Majestic overlooking the Zócalo, with stunning panoramic views of the city.

Traditional Mexican cuisine from various regions. Expect dishes like mole oaxqueno and if you're adventurous, chapulines. Pleasant outdoor patio on a plaza made for people watching. Mariachis on weekends.

Many places in the Centro Histórico boast of the views from their rooftop dining rooms, but Miralto in the 41st floor of the Torre Latinoamericana looks down on all of them. Best views of any dining room in the city. Traditional Mexican…
Azul offers upscale Mexican cuisine in a romantic Centro courtyard with lush trees and stone archways.

Elegant restaurant serving a fusion of contemporary Mexican cuisine with flavors and ingredients from Africa and India. Dishes are often unusual combinations like a paratha quesadilla, or a chai tres leches. Service is top notch.…

Rooftop dining atop the Hotel Zocalo Central. Food is nouveau Mexican with a number of unusual and creative fusions. The 9-course tasting menu is recommended because it highlights small plates showcasing various chef selections. The…
The original and most famous Mexican cantina, traditional home to the bohemians and mariachis of the 40s and 50s. Huge selection of tequila and mezcal, light Mexican food, and mariachi bands.
Traditional bar dating back to the Porfiriato era (est. 1870), it's ornate and impressive to see, but a fun place to have a beer or a cocktail. Serves food.

Old school traditional cantina where the tequila is strong and the men drink lots of it. They have mezcal and other liquors as well, but tequila is king here with more than 150 brands at your call! Free botanas (including tacos and…
Casual place with good baguette sandwiches and dark draft beer.

While the lightweights are nursing their hangovers on Sunday, the hardcore head to Mexico City's biggest Sunday night party where the house keeps rocking until 2am. The biggest crowds hit after midnight.
Friendly traditional cantina since 1928. Popular place to watch a soccer game or hang out and drink beer. Serves traditional Mexican food.

eat.h: Mon-Fri 13:00 - 20:00, Fri-Sat 13:00 - 10:30 (yep, they close for 2-1/2 hours to clean up)
eat.b: Old school cantina that celebrates the hispanic tradition of bullfighting. Campy wall decorations, a great jukebox full of classic Mexican rancheras, rock en espanol, and pop hits of the 90s. Cheap tacos, great variety of mezcal and…

Dim, smoky bar with a hipster crowd. No sign, so you need to know where it is then look for the curtain across the doorway. Go in and join the crowd in sampling one of the city's widest selection of mezcals.
Traditional cantina with an early 20th-century vibe. Friendly atmosphere, occasional mariachis.

Friendly and colorful traditional pulqueria (one of the most popular in the city) with murals on the ceiling and walls. Serves cured and white (blanco) pulques. Try a natural pulque to taste pure agave flavor, or try one of the fruit or…

eat.a: Eligio Ancona 122, Santa Maria La Ribera
eat.b: This used to be the Xochitl Pulqueria, but it changed hands in 2020 while keeping the tacky decor and the limited menu of just the pulques, only the pulques, and nothing but pulques, so help me God. Natural and curadas are available…
Wonderfully tacky flaming gay bar with drag queens and strippers for entertainment, no cover charge for anyone, and some delicious house mezcal drinks. Try the El Mayate --- minty and refreshing!
Delightfully tacky strip shows and disco balls. Very friendly crowd.

In business at the same location since 1930, this is Mexico City's oldest coffee house. They roast their own beans, specializing in organic Mexican-grown coffees. Cups of joe are also available for as little as M$15. The Cafe…
Good coffee drinks plus hot chocolate and tea. Light food available including baked goods and vegetarian dishes like ratatouille.

eat.pr: M$69–140 for breakfast packages, coffee from M$30
eat.b: Opened in 1952, this iconic café is a nostalgic gem, steeped in history as a meeting place for revolutionaries like Fidel Castro and Che Guevara, who reportedly planned the Cuban Revolution here, and literary giants like Gabriel García…

eat.a: Lago Mayor, Secc. II, Bosque de Chapultepec
eat.b: Elegant lakeside dining in Chapultepec park, outdoor dining area available. Menu is more American or European than Mexican, which may appeal to some travelers. Reservations accepted.

eat.a: Lago Menor, Del Rosal s/n, Bosque De Chapultepec
eat.b: Casual upscale dining with traditional Mexican cuisine. The restaurant is in Chapultepec Park, with a lakeside setting. The dining rooms features a glass wall with views of the lake right outside the restaurant.

eat.a: Av. de los Corredores S/N, Sección II, Bosque de Chapultepec
eat.b: Casual outdoor cafe specializing in coffee and breakfast. Popular with runners and dog walkers alike. Very pet friendly with an area set aside for customers with well-behaved, leashed dogs.

eat.a: Bosque de Chapultepec, Pista El Sope S/N, Bosque de Chapultepec II Secc
eat.b: Sophisticated upscale dining in a landmark of modern architecture built on the edge of one of the lakes in Chapultepec Park. A cross between elegant dining and a cultural center that includes a gallery of contemporary art and spaces for…

This is a charming and luxurious restaurant which serves slightly expensive Italian fare that is surprisingly worth it. Be sure to try the Fettuccine Alfredo or the Torre de Pisa, which is mouth-wateringly delicious.
Small traditional restaurant serving antojitos and other light fare. The house specialty is roasted pork shoulder tacos.

eat.a: Calle Gob.Protasio Tagle 66A, San Miguel Chapultepec II Secc
eat.b: Deliciously fascinating fusion of nouveau Mexican cuisine and Indian cuisine served in an elegantly sparse contemporary dining room. While the sabudana vada is recommended, most dishes will be unfamiliar to diners so a wise approach is…

eat.a: Calle Gral. Fco. Molinos del Campo 19
eat.b: Small streetside cafe with a few tables outside on the sidewalk and more upstairs on a 2nd floor balcony. Wide range of pastries and baked goods, including several options for vegans. Excellent coffee.
Casual Argentinian steakhouse that also serves seafood.

eat.a: Boulevard Manuel Ávila Camacho Norte Conjunto
eat.b: Steakhouse offering a variety of grilled meats including picaña, ribeyes and more. A buffet offers salads, pastas, soup, and traditional Mexican dishes.
Inexpensive casual restaurant serving traditional Mexican cuisine including arrachera, pozole and enchiladas. Homemade desserts.
Casual restaurant serving traditional Mexican dishes including chile en nogada, milanesa, and various styles of chicken. The ribeye sandwich is both big and delicious.
Basic corporate-style chain bar with several imported beers available. Dart boards and TVs tuned to sports games. Unexciting, but generically inoffensive.

Reasonably priced Asian/Italian fusion with a Mexican touch, good bar and good coffee. The staff is laid back to the point of being unprofessional, don't worry about asking twice for your order. Try the pasta with chicken and sesame…
Lebanese meze restaurant serving grilled meats like kebabs and all your Middle Eastern favorites like hummus and tabouleh. Very popular.
Argentinian cuisine run by an Argentine owner, very good food at a very reasonable price. The bar is very popular at night.

This hip cafe has some good food and a pervasive retro look. Billing itself as a cafe recreativo, it's got sudoku and word searches on the placemats, and pencils and scratch paper on every table; help yourself to the wall of board games…

eat.a: Fernando Montes de Oca 86, Col. Condesa
eat.b: Vibrant small rooftop restaurant in Condesa with innovative dishes that couple traditional Mexican dishes with unusual accompaniments and flavors. Editors of the Michelin Guide reserved their highest praise for the fresh fish entrees.
This fast-food place serves rolled sandwiches using flat thin white bread. Wide choice of salads.
Fresh salads made to order with fresh greens and other ingredients. Ten locations in D.F. When you're missing fresh veggies, this is the place to go!
The club serves Middle Eastern food and flavored tobacco "hookahs" at your table. The music selection is extremely good ranging from Electro-arabic, to house.

This family-run restaurant is one of the cheapest places in the city to have good Argentinian/Uruguayan food. Start with some Provolone cheese and papas con amor (fried potato wedges with the peel still on). If you're hungry, also try…

Creative Mediterranean food in a stylish restaurant owned by celebrity chef Elena Reygadas. Wood-burning oven. Lively corner location with open windows, plants and lots of light. Many unusual contemporary Mexican dishes like the insects…
Popular sidewalk coffee shop. Homemade pastries and outstanding people watching.

Chic contemporary Mexican restaurant with an upscale clientele and a reputation for sustainable business practices that earned them a coveted green star in the 2025 Michelin Guide. The restaurant is not a "vegan" restaurant, but they…

Innovative upscale restaurant serving nouveau Mexican cuisine in an intimate setting. Service is top-notch and waiters will patiently guide diners through the sometimes unusual dishes. The tomahawk pork chops are big enough to share but…
A slice of Italy just a couple blocks from Chapultepec Park. Pizzas, homemade pastas, veal piccata, in-house bakery, gelatos and an excellent wine selection.
A counter-culture vegan restaurant specializing in mushroom preparations and fermentation of all sorts, with inspiration from indigenous dishes.
Classic Jewish deli with in-house bakery serving huge sandwiches. Assortment of bagels made fresh daily.

Popular taco chain with various locations in Mexico City. A little overpriced, but very high quality tacos. The specialty is the gaonera (try the one with cheese), a large, thin slice of tender beef, roasted and placed on a tortilla.…

This small cafe offers excellent food at very low prices until 18:00. A set dinner includes a soup, a salad, a main dish, a small dessert, fruit flavored water, and coffee. The pasta dishes are good and portions are abundant.
Tasty authentic Japanese food at good prices in a very warm, randomly decorated place. A nice spot to hang out and have a drink or coffee/tea also. Impressive tea selection.
Serves very good flautas and tacos de guisado. Delivery available.
Hugely popular upscale seafood restaurant. Reservations recommended (can be made on opentable.com). Locals recommend the tuna tostadas.

Lively fresh seafood restaurant with a wide range of innovative dishes. Excellent cocktails. Live music. Both indoor and outdoor dining areas (outdoor is sometimes more peaceful if you want to be away from the music).
Trendy upscale restaurant serving nouveau Mexican cuisine. Modern, tranquil dining room. Good drinks, wide variety of dishes including beef, seafood, lamb and more.
